This is a continuation from the final episode of *The Spear Hero’s Second Chance*. It’s the “True Tutorial” arc.
=====
“Father! Big Sister! Filo-oooooo! Wait for meeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!”
I barely managed to catch up to Father’s cart as it raced away. But after glancing at me with a face like he’d just swallowed a bitter pill, he turned his gaze forward with a tense expression.
“Filo! Run faster!”
“G-Guaaaaaaaah!”
Filo-tan showed some real grit at Father’s request! This is it! She’s actually enjoying this game of tag with me! Woaaaaah, I won’t lose!
Just as I was thinking that and showing off my leg strength to Filo-tan and my Father, the cart jolted, and the figure sitting on the back looked like it was about to tumble off. Oh, that’s my sister! Isn’t that a little dangerous?
“Raphtalia! Are you okay!?”
“U… uh…”
She looked completely drained and was about to fall off at any moment. She seems to be in pretty bad shape.
“Here we go!”
I gave her a gentle shove to get her back onto the cart, then hopped on myself.
“I caught up to you! I win this game of tag!”
“Tch… He’s not even out of breath.”
And so, my father pulled on the reins and stopped Filo-chan. Then, while holding his shield in a defensive stance, he kept glancing over at my sister. What kind of reaction is this, I wonder?
“What’s the matter?”
“Send Raphtalia over here.”
“Yes, sir. She doesn’t look well.”
Following Father’s instructions, I handed my sister over to him. Seeing my attitude, my Father furrowed his brow and tilted his head.
“Would you like me to cast an anti-nausea spell or a Recovery spell?”
“Are you planning to make Raphtalia drink poison!?”
Poison? Why on earth would I need to make my Older Sister drink poison? If anyone’s going to drink it, it should be the Crimson Swine. I’d like to make him drink a poison that makes him writhe in agony, just like what he did to Fleon-chan. Well, he’s already out of this world, though. HAHAHA.
“I wouldn’t do such a thing. You don’t look too well, so you should probably get some rest.”
“You’re the one saying that! Who do you think is to blame for us having to run away!?”
Let me think about it. …No matter how I look at it, I can’t think of anyone but Crimson Swine!
“It’s Crimson Swine’s fault! I’ll never forgive that guy!”
“No! It’s your fault for killing him!”
“Hahaha, wasn’t it because you, Father, demanded I take him out?”
“I never said that! I was just thinking it!”
Oh, he’s even more hostile than the Father in my memories. In my hazy memories, my Father used to sigh a lot when talking to me and always seemed gloomy. However, it’s the greatest honor to be able to sense what’s really on his mind. I’ll keep this up and prove myself to be his right-hand man!
“Well, the Lazy Pig got away, but that’s a trivial matter.”
“What do you mean, a trivial matter…? Are you really okay? In every way?”
As he said that, my Father looked at me with concern. This Motoyasu—tears of emotion are welling up in my eyes. Unlike in the previous loop, you still have a kind heart that wants to be closer to the Father from the first world! That’s exactly the kind of Father you are. I’ll follow you wherever you go!
“Oh! That worried look in Father’s eyes! I, Motoyasu, am truly delighted!”
“That’s why I told you to stop fooling around!　Oh, for heaven’s sake!”
“Guh?”
Oh? Filo-chan seems concerned about us and is looking this way, glancing around. Leave it to me, Filo-chan. I’ll definitely show you the path to glory alongside my Father… the Filolial Road.
“Ugh… w-what happened?”
My sister, who had been slumped over, opened her eyes and turned toward Father. Then, realizing I was there, she staggered and tried to stand up hurriedly. Her expression was pained, but it was also clearly on guard. Hmm… Why am I being treated with such suspicion?
“Actually, a little while ago… when Filo kicked Motoyasu—who was laughing his head off—that bastard snapped, started babbling nonsense, and went and killed that woman right in front of me.”
“Huh!? R-really!?”
“Yeah, I’m not exaggerating. He really did kill her with that spear.”
The older sister looked at me with a shocked expression. So, I gave a firm nod. It’s an undeniable fact, after all. The Crimson Swine is a being unworthy of living in this world. In fact, the longer he stays alive, the more vitality is drained from the world.
“I’m not lying, you know? I killed that scourge of the world, the Crimson Swine!”
The surprised Older Sister looked at my Father, and he nodded silently. She’s still staring at me with a look that says she can’t believe it. All right, I should have made it clear by now that I’m on her side. From here on out, I’ll prove that I’m someone she can trust.
“The orders of my Father are absolute. That’s the condition for making you part of our team, after all.”
“Father? Naofumi-sama, did you set a condition for letting him join us?”
“I didn’t say that! He’s been acting like this the whole time. Can’t you do something about it?!”
My father is running his fingers through his hair. You’ll damage your cuticles if you keep doing that!
“W-what on earth… What do you mean, ‘strange’?”
“I’ve come from the future, and I know everything. The shock from earlier brought it all back to me.”
“The future…?”
My Older Sister is looking at me with furrowed brows. Well, I suppose it’s hard to make her believe me right away. But I’ll keep talking patiently, just like in the previous loop. Because I believe that’s the true path to peace.
“So you knew all that and still killed him?”
“He’s a menace—there’s not the slightest reason to let him live.”
“Well, I agree with that… but I’ll be the one taking the blame for killing that woman, won’t I!”
“Is there a problem with taking the blame?”
“Of course there is! You’re planning to frame me again, aren’t you?!”
Oh? Father’s reaction… Ah, come to think of it, he doesn’t know the real reason why he’s been framed. In that case, I suppose I’d best start by explaining that.
“Um, what do you mean by ‘Father’?”
“Because you’re Filo-chan’s Father, of course.”
“Guh?”
“Filo’s… well, considering your relationship with Naofumi-sama, I suppose you could be considered Filo’s foster father…”
It seems my sister is also starting to recover from her motion sickness.
“So, Father, don’t you want to know why you were falsely accused of rape?”
At my question, Father glared at me intensely while clenching his fists. Then, as if choosing his words carefully, he said:
“…What do you know? What are you trying to say with that mocking attitude?”
“It’s the truth I learned from the future. Of course, the things I did without realizing it are facts that can’t be changed, but I’m truly remorseful.”
“Just spit it out. Well… since you wiped that guy out, I suppose I might as well hear you out a little.”
“You believe me!?”
“You can’t just pull off a massacre right in front of me and get away with a ‘Hehehe, just kidding.’ At the very least, the Motoyasu I’ve known up until now would never have done something like that.”
“That’s… true.”
Just as I expected from my Father. You really do know me well. My sister seems convinced, too. It’s true—the me before I recalled my memories of the future would never have killed Crimson Swine. I’ll use this as a breakthrough to gain their trust!
“Whether I end up messing up again or manage to get away with this, since Filo ran after me and caught up, I have no choice but to listen to what he has to say.”
He’s quick to assess the situation. I’d like to learn from that.
“Then I’ll tell you. This country, Melromarc, has a state religion that regards the Shield Hero as the enemy.”

“What!?”

Oh, Filo-chan… the way you tilt your little head like that is absolutely adorable! I’d love to record that voice on a sound-recording crystal and listen to it 24 hours a day, 365 days a year! When do you sleep? HAHAHA, I’d want to listen to it even while you’re sleeping.
Plus, in the future, your schedule was so busy you couldn’t even meet me, but it seems you’re not quite that busy right now. I’d really like to get along well with you, Filo-chan. But before that, I’ll have to get permission from your Father. I’ll have to explain things thoroughly.

My father is keeping a wary eye on me while consulting with my sister. I guess he still doesn’t believe me.
“Well, it wasn’t my head that got hit—it was my groin… So, is that silly saying true—that a womanizer’s brain is in his groin…?”
My father is wearing a rather ambiguous expression. This isn’t looking good. At this rate, he might not trust me. Alright, how about I get my sister to help persuade him too?
“Big Sister”
“Eh… Based on the order in which we’ve been taking care of Naofumi-sama, does that mean I’m ‘Big Sister’ because I’m Filo’s Older Sister?”

As expected of Big Sister, you’re very perceptive. You are, after all, Filo-chan’s Older Sister.

Oh? That backfired, didn’t it? Big Sis’s guard is up now. I feel like my Father from the first world is saying, “You’re still just as stupid as ever.” That’s not true! I’m not stupid! I’m just faithful to love!

“So I just missed the mark and ended up looking like an idiot after all…”
“Please wait! Please hear me out! I made a mistake!”
“We’ll see about that…”
Come on, R'yne! I’m experiencing an endorphin rush! Ha… Knowledge from a loop I experienced before raced through my mind, and a brilliant idea struck me.
“I know the names of the villagers where my older sister used to live, and I know she has an Older Sister!”
“Oh, really… Does Raphtalia have an Older Sister?”
Huh? My father seems interested. She’s here, she’s here. The Older Sister of that super-strong orca therianthrope’s Older Sister.
“An Older Sister?”
“Doesn’t she have one?”
“She must have one! She’s the Older Sister of that orca therianthrope who used Lightning Magic and worked as a fisherman in the neighborhood!”
“Hmm… Could you be referring to Sadeena? I’ve heard that her parents cherished her like a daughter, and to me, she was like a sister.”
“You could look that up later, couldn’t you? Like, after being rejected by Raphtalia, you just can’t let it go and decide to dig into her background.”
Guh… I suppose that’s not entirely out of the question. Then my Father started whispering with my older sister. But with these enhanced ears—the Motoyasu Ears—I can pick up even the faintest whispers! Motoyasu Ears! Full Drive!
“What do you think?”
Alright, I can make out every word perfectly. This means I’m not left out of the loop anymore!
“It’s way too outlandish to be a lie… Motoyasu isn’t an idiot… no, normally he’d tell a much better lie, right?”
“Why did you stop halfway through?”
“If that wasn’t an act, then he’s just a complete idiot right now.”
“…You’re right.”
“Or rather, was it the future…? If he really could use such a powerful skill, it does make you wonder why he didn’t use it in the duel…”
Of course, there’s no way I could have used Brionac at that point. I knew from the game’s lore that I’d eventually be able to use it, though. It’s a shameful past—I foolishly turned my blade against my Father, who had such low attack power, and ended up losing. On top of that, the Crimson Swine used underhanded tactics to tarnish the sacred duel. He’s gone now, but he was a filthy scum of a man—no matter how many times I killed him, it still wouldn’t have been enough.
Anyway, I turned over a new leaf and swore to fight for the peaceful world that Father and Filo are striving for. This oath is an eternal pact that will never falter—not even after the world achieves peace… or even if a new loop begins!
“W-well, if you have some sort of plan, that’s fine…”
“But you’re not planning to kill that woman or make Filo your bride, are you? You don’t seem to have any intention of convincing us.”
“It’s strange in so many ways, isn’t it? As for whether that story about you coming from the future is actually true… why don’t you test it out a little more?”
“Hmm… Well… I do have a slight hunch. What should I do…? It’s a revelation that the unreasonable things happening to me are actually caused by religion, but…”
You seem troubled. I suppose there’s nothing to be done about it.
“Then, as proof that I’m joining you, I’ll hand over my entire fortune.”
I reached into my pocket and handed my Father a money pouch. I don’t know how much is in it, but it’s just pocket change anyway. Since I’m going to be handing over all my money to my Father anyway, if this helps me gain even a little trust, it’s a win. My Father took my money and his eyes widened even more.
“You’re just going to say it got stolen, aren’t you!”
“I won’t say that. If I did, Father and Filo would end up hating me. If you want, I’ll earn more and bring it back.”
If I can build trust with money, so be it. Here we go—the tribute! Tribute, tribute—a mountain of gold coins!
“……”
At my words, my Father fell silent and began checking the contents of the money bag. Given that it’s been a few days since the first wave ended, there should be a decent amount in there. Well, I figure I could easily earn this much by wiping out griffins in the mountains or hunting down bandits. I’ll work like a workhorse to contribute to you, Father! The fact that the “workhorse” analogy shares a common spirit with Lady Filolial is quite appealing.
“So, Father. What should we do next?”

Unfortunately, I’m not very familiar with that sort of thing, but it might be possible. After all, people fighting each other is a constant in history. But I’d hate to see a future like that. If that were actually true, we’d absolutely have to prevent it.

It’s my father’s consideration, I suppose—even a hero would collapse if they worked day and night without a break. By the way, my Father from the first world also let me take breaks fairly often.

Happy New Year. I look forward to working with you again this year.
=====
The next day. I guess I have no choice—I’ll be using a portal to travel with my Father to the meeting spot with my Rival. We’ve got a bunch of diplomatic engagements lined up in Melromarc, after all. The main purpose is to hear about the issues regarding Trash and the results of the investigation. While I’m at it, I’d better ask him to arrange a visit to Cal Mira Island as well. With that in mind, as I was waiting in front of the mountain near Rival’s parents’ house—our meeting spot—…
“I’m home!”
Rival arrived, flying in the form of a dragon.
“Um…”
“……”
And for some reason, she’s brought along her Assistant, who’s got an incredibly intense glare in her eyes. The Assistant, still cradled in Rival’s arms, has been glaring at us the whole time. Father is pointing at Rival.
“My big sister insisted on coming along and wouldn’t let go, so I brought her with me.”
“I found you! You little sister thieves! How dare you steal my little sister!”
Just as the Assistant said that, Rival quickly turned her back to hide the Assistant. She’s getting right to it, isn’t she?
“Big sis, that’s not what we agreed on. You’re not supposed to say things like that to Naofumi and the others.”
“But it’s the truth.”
“Hmm… That’s why I’ve explained it so many times. Gaelion chose to go with Naofumi and the others on her own.”
“But you said that name is Dad’s name!”
“I told you this, too. It’s a name given to Gaelion by a big sister from a different future.”
“But you’re still you.”
“Ugh, seriously… this is such a hassle… It’s not like Gaelion has started hating you or turned into a different dragon—he’s just out and about.”
“After making him grow this big, you’re still going to say that?”
It seems they’re still arguing about something. Heh heh heh, I think this would be a good opportunity to reveal the Rival’s true identity to my Father.
“Big Sis, Gaelion is a rising star. He’s an incredibly strong, invincible dragon. He’s a bit full of himself, but he only got to where he is thanks to Naofumi and the others.”
“What’s going to happen to our lives?”
“Well, I brought him some treats yesterday and gave him a territory, so Dad seemed satisfied.”
“Oh… that, huh.”
The Assistant seems genuinely off her rocker. She’s referring to her parent as “that.” I seem to recall that the Assistant from past loops actually respected her parent.
“Big sis, you should tone down your contempt for Dad a bit. He was really depressed when you hated him.”
“A dragon without pride who sacrificed his own daughter just to save his own skin.”
“Big sis, face the facts. Dad’s such a pathetic dragon that he can even call himself the Weakest Dragon Emperor. It’s too late now.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
The panda chimes in. With that, Rival turned around, forcing a smile.
“I’ll definitely get my little sister back!”
“Even though she looks so different now, you can still recognize Gaelion-chan as your little sister, huh?”
“Of course! You little sister-stealers! I’ve heard what you did to my little sister. You came from another world? So what?!”
“From the perspective of someone stuck in a loop, is this actually a welcome reaction?”
My father looks a bit puzzled. I’m not really sure. In most worlds, my fathers accept me without issue, so I haven’t really felt anything out of the ordinary.
“Big sis, shh…”
“Ah, wait a minute!”
Rival covers the Assistant’s mouth with her hand before explaining to my fathers.
“She went home to win a turf war and improve her parents’ lives. Separately from that, my big sister had fallen ill.”
“Hmm, I can kind of tell just by looking at her. It seems she really isn’t okay after all.”
“It seems she took my brother and sisters with her to hunt monsters and train in search of strength. Apparently, she was trying her best to get Gaelion back. She must have been pretty energetic, because her territory had gotten quite large.”
This loop’s Assistant seems quite aggressive, doesn’t she? To think she was acting like some sort of monster tamer while leading her siblings around… Come to think of it, she was chosen as one of the Vassal Weapons in the first world, wasn’t she? Maybe she really did have a knack for it.
“And… she seems to be convinced that Dad handed over Gaelion just to save his own life, so she’d lost her dignity and was feeling down.”
“Your parents have been pathetic for a while now.”
“I won’t deny it.”
“No, let’s just deny that part.”
After all, they’re parent dragons. It’s too late to be pathetic now. If anything, Rival is the most troublesome of the lot.
“So, just as I was about to leave—thinking it was time to go—my big sister refused to budge, insisting she’d absolutely come with me, so I ended up having to look after her for a while. Even Dad couldn’t refuse, given Gaelion’s strength.”
“Well… if that’s what it takes to satisfy her, isn’t that fine? Though… is it really okay to take her to Shieldfreeden…?”
“My big sis has a certain wild instinct, so she’s sensitive. I think she’ll be fine once I do a Class Up on her.”
That’s a pretty casual way of putting it.
“To begin with, my big sis…”
The Rival spreads his arms wide and speaks to the Assistant with a serious expression, as if trying to reason with him.
“No matter how hard you try, Big Sis, you’re not a dragon… Dad was planning to send you back to the human world eventually. That won’t change even with Gaelion. Are you… aware of that?”
“……”
The Assistant remains silent, her brows furrowed conspicuously. It feels like the kind of thing you know deep down, but it’s still unpleasant when it’s thrown in your face.
“No matter how things turn out, if Dad were to be killed in some incident, Big Sister’s life would be over. To prevent that, Big Sister was scheduled to leave the nest soon. Gaelion was entrusted to her as a younger sister to help with that.”
Having said that, my rival gazes at my Father with a distant, somewhat lonely look in her eyes. Hahaha, that look won’t work on me. It’s useless trying to elicit my sympathy.
“…Originally, Gaelion was supposed to die without fulfilling that role, and my older sister…”
After a moment, my Rival shook her head slightly and said to her Assistant:
“My older sister is going to experience the human world alongside Gaelion. After all, the world is currently facing an unprecedented crisis, and that’s why Gaelion is working hard alongside everyone else.”
“A newborn little sister’s job is to grow up playing!”
“She’s already had plenty of fun and grown up by now! From now on, I’m going to show my big sister some difficult and fun toys… I’m going to show her the world!”
Does that mean she’s going to turn the world into a toy!? She’s a real piece of work.
“Gaelion, that sounds like it’d be really bad for that kid’s education. Are you sure it’s okay?”
“I kind of get the feeling something’s off here.”
“No doubt about it.”
“Please don’t nitpick my words. Anyway, big sis, you’re going to keep your promise. Otherwise, I’m leaving you behind right here.”
The Rival seized the moment to intimidate the Assistant. The Assistant then looked over at us with a reluctant expression and said:
“My name is Wyndia… May I… stay with you for a while?”
Father looked at Rival, then shifted his gaze to the Assistant and nodded.
“Yeah, sure. Gaelion, make sure to protect her well.”
“It’s a big sister’s job to protect her little sister!”
“Big sis, you know Gaelion is stronger right now. In the wild, strength determines the hierarchy. Whether you’re the older or younger sister, that’s an undeniable fact.”
“……”
Hmm… I see. Her pride as an older sister is getting the better of her, I suppose. Honestly, the Assistant right now would be knocked out by a single flick from the Rival.
“Well then… since you probably don’t want to face us, make sure you don’t stray from Gaelion-chan, okay? And you know, I didn’t exactly ‘steal’ Gaelion-chan—I’m just borrowing her strength. So, whenever Gaelion-chan wants to go home, I’ll send her right back.”
“That would make me a little lonely, though—”
Rival is seizing this chance to make his move, but Father isn’t falling for your temptations anymore! He’s got an elephant and a panda, after all. Father is a man of integrity. The assistant looked back and forth between my Father and the Rival, then nodded.
“I understand… I look forward to working with you from now on.”
It seems the assistant has accepted Father’s instructions, as he’s sticking close to the Rival and tagging along with us. And so, we headed to the castle in Melromarc.
---
“Thank you very much for joining us at this meeting in Melromarc.”
The queen opened the meeting with a greeting. Representing Siltvelt were my father and the elders of the Shusaku and Genmu clans. Representing Shieldfreeden was Rival.
It seems this meeting is for a progress report on that Trash who escaped and to discuss matters related to Éclair’s family. Officially, it’s a discussion aimed at building friendly relations, and it seems they need the pretext that Shieldfreeden is cooperating.
There are various other matters as well, so I absolutely must have a talk with the Queen. Whenever they have a spare moment, Sakura-chan and Filolial-sama go visit their Finacées. I’d like to go hang out with Filolial-sama, too.
“Regarding this report… well, as for the impostor claiming to be the Wise King of Wisdom who escaped from our castle… we still haven’t been able to locate him. We can only lament our own shortcomings.”
“No… please don’t worry about it…”
After all, rather than just being good at hiding, there are some shady characters involved. Still, I wonder where Trash is hiding. By the way, my assistant can’t quite wrap his head around the situation and is looking around nervously while sitting on Rival’s lap.
“Still… it’s actually pretty impressive that we still can’t find him…”
“Even though people from our country are cooperating in the search…”
I hear that a tracking team from Siltvelt is also taking various actions. And yet, he still can’t be found… Could he have just died alone somewhere? If he were to show up as a ghost, I’d take it as nothing but a joke. HAHAHA.
“In any case, please do not let your guard down.”
“Yeah. Also, as a countermeasure against the one impersonating the Wise King, I’ve been told that the subordinates of Larsazusa—my guardian knight—will lend a hand. Please discuss this later when I’m not around.”
I heard that if the tiger siblings were to meet Father, it would cause problems within Siltvelt. Thanks to the medical care, the tiger girl has made a full recovery, and she’s been going out here and there, carried on the tiger boy’s back. She says she can walk, but it seems she hasn’t tried it yet. Well, I think the Queen will understand the situation just by seeing the tiger girl.
“Understood. By the way, is Knight Éclair able to be of assistance to the Heroes?”
“Yes, absolutely… I believe it is thanks to her that Melromarc and Siltvelt have been able to maintain friendly relations despite these events.”
It seems my Father is praising Éclair with the highest possible praise.
“Therefore, I would very much like you to prioritize the reconstruction of Knight Eclair’s domain.”
“As requested by Siltvelt, we are currently working at a rapid pace to rebuild the Seaetto domain. We are continuing various projects, starting with the protection of those who were targeted in the slave raids.”
“That’s the most important thing.”
It seems the people from Big Sister’s village are also being protected and are in the process of rebuilding. It’s a shame we can’t carry out that sort of work in this loop. Couldn’t you convince him by pointing to Éclair’s military exploits and saying Father is urging him to help?
Well… I understand why it’s better not to tell Big Sister—as Rival mentioned. After all, she was so shaken when she found out my sister had passed away. Back then, she managed to pull through thanks to Father’s passion, but if she were to learn the truth upon meeting him for the first time and fall ill again, even Father wouldn’t be able to be that firm.
It’s frustrating, isn’t it…? Since lies won’t work on Big Sister’s older sister, it’s impossible to keep deceiving her. Having this knowledge of the loop is incredibly inconvenient.
“Oh, right. Some good news from within our kingdom of Melromarc: I’ve heard that Sakura-sama of Filolial—whom my daughter Melty and the Heroes are taking care of—is gaining popularity thanks to the publicity efforts at taverns across the land, including the nobles’ soirées.”
The Queen reports this to me with a smile. Oh… Is my Finacée spreading Sakura-chan’s popularity throughout Melromarc? It’s truly fitting of a Finacée that things have turned out this way even though I didn’t say anything in particular. It’s frustrating, but I have no choice but to acknowledge her character and abilities.

"The plot goes like this: Princess Melty secretly performs music, and with Sakura of Filolial as her partner, they spread the word through song to protect Melromarc, Siltvelt, Shieldfreeden—and ultimately the entire world—from the waves engulfing the world and the remnants of the evil pseudo-hero Takt… and is spreading word of this crisis through her songs…”
“Well, well… it seems the Queen of Melromarc has a truly reliable successor.”
The elders of the Shusaku and Genmu clans both offered the Queen their customary words of praise.
“Well then, our nation cannot afford to lag behind forever. I earnestly request that you, the Shield Hero, along with Knight Larsazusa and the other Guardian Knights, do your utmost. It’s about time we increased our ranks as well.”
“Y-yeah, you’re right.”
I heard this later from my Father: apparently, he seized this opportunity to imply a request for us to have children behind those words. Even I found that one hard to pick up on.
“In that regard, as a future task—and since Faubrey has also made a request—I’d like to coordinate our efforts regarding the protection of the Sword Hero.”
It seems the Queen has shifted from a lighthearted topic to a serious one. Is this about Ren’s protection? Come to think of it, I haven’t seen him since returning to this loop. Last time, he was erased by Takt, so it feels like it’s been quite a while since I last saw him.
“Due to the blunder committed by our nation, Melromarc, we’ve lost the trust of others, and the whereabouts of the Sword Hero remain unknown. Based on the Spear Hero’s testimony, we’ve requested that Zeltoble conduct a search there as well, and searches are currently underway in various nations, but he has not yet been found.”
All eyes turned to me. So Ren still hasn’t been found, huh? In the loop where we stayed in Melromarc, he would’ve slipped back in under the guise of a righteous hero, taking advantage of the commotion when the queen returned.
“Hasn’t he shown up yet?”
Just how distrustful of people is she? Well, perhaps it’s partly because we weren’t torn to shreds by Trash during the first wave we participated in back then. Ren has a tendency to be unnecessarily stubborn, after all. Objectively speaking, being told to keep your distance might feel different from being told to your face that you’re not trying hard enough.
“Yes… I had intended to have the country’s shadow forces search as well, but since the Hero can teleport…”
When the Portal skill is used, even the Shadow finds it difficult to track him. If I recall correctly, I heard that in the first world—and especially as we began using portals for travel across various loops—the Shadow often ended up confined to monitoring our bases.
“I hope we can find him somewhere and have a talk…”
“Well, I think the Sword Hero of this loop would at least be willing to listen to what we have to say.”
Our Rival seizes the moment and raises his hand to speak.
“Gaelion is trying to lure out the Sword Hero here… no, wait—he might already be here, so I won’t say anything.”
“What might that be, Lord Gaelion, the representative dragon of Shieldfreeden?”
Guh… Even the Queen is addressing my Rival with the honorific “Lord”! This guy’s got his head in the clouds. Everyone, don’t be fooled!
“The Sword Hero is a level-grinding addict and a level-obsessed fanatic. Even if such a guy is hiding out, the ‘honey’ he’d produce should be in season right now in this country!”
The Queen nodded as if convinced by Rival’s proposal and hid her mouth with her fan. Ah, I see. Indeed, Ren would probably show up.
“It’s Cal Mira Island, isn’t it!”
“I see… revitalizing Cal Mira Island, huh… It certainly wouldn’t be surprising if the Hero were mingling among them.”
“Exactly. How about we bring in Naofumi and the others from Siltvelt to join us and boost our combat strength?”
“Wouldn’t it have been more efficient for us if Gaelion-chan had fought at sea?”
“That’s exactly why we need a small, elite force. If we use Cal Mira Island, we can boost our numbers significantly—even with the level cap.”
“…I see. Considering what lies ahead, it can’t hurt to go. It’s important, especially with the remnants of the Takt faction and such to consider.”
The representatives from Siltvelt, including the Queen, are nodding in agreement. This is a great opportunity. I’m going to buy up all the Filolial-sama and increase my numbers, too.
“And while we’re at it, Spear Hero. Since you’re the type who’s probably already thinking about increasing your Filolial-sama count anyway, this is the perfect chance.”
Dammit… that Rival of mine is throwing salt in my face again! Don’t read my mind!
“I’ll do it even without you telling me!”
“Now, now… Anyway, it’s a good spot to lure out Ren, who’s hiding somewhere and can’t be found.”
“Exactly. He might already be on the island.”
“Got it. Still… is it okay if I stay on the island and look for him?”
“Father, I’m here too, you know?”
For some reason, my father brushed me off.
“Motoyasu, you want to train more Filolials, don’t you? It’d be a problem if we had too many right now, but since it’s what you want to do, I suppose it’s fine.”
What?! So that suggestion was actually made with me in mind! But I need to be careful here.
“Rival, you’re planning to go after my Father while I’m away, aren’t you?!”
Then, for some reason, Rival waved his hand sideways and acted like he was refusing.
“It’s a bit of a shame, but I have diplomatic engagements in Gaelion scheduled, so I won’t be able to join you until later.”
“Is something up?”
“Yeah. The Queen of Melromarc and the representative from Siltvelt—I’d like you to hear them out. The seal on the Spirit Tortoise is about to be broken soon. So, to minimize the number of victims, how about we engage in diplomacy with that country?”
Huh? So my Rival isn’t coming to Cal Mira Island after all? This is a stroke of luck! A vacation on a southern island with my Father and the others! Yippee! The hot sun and the blue sea are calling us!
“…You’re right. It might be a good idea to make a proposal in advance.”
“If it can reduce the casualties, there’s no reason not to do it.”
“Lord Gaelion, Representative of Shieldfreeden, are you aware of the time limit for the Spirit Tortoise’s seal?”
“Of course I am. If the heroes don’t get involved, I know exactly when the seal will be broken. I’d like to take care of this while the Sword Hero is still under the honey’s spell.”
It seems the discussion has progressed quite a bit.
“Do we have to participate?”
At this point, Father asks the Queen and his Rival if he feels some sort of obligation. In response, the representatives all make grim faces and shake their heads.
“Honestly, we’d prefer to avoid sending the Heroes on a diplomatic mission to that country…”
“That country is arguably the most corrupt and exclusive of all. If the Heroes were to visit, who knows what they might do, taking advantage of the situation…”
“Unless it’s a matter the Heroes absolutely insist on handling, I think we should avoid it.”
Hmm… Was it really such a troubled country? Well, I did go in based on what I knew from the game at first. I headed straight for the Spirit Tortoise’s seal, which was my target. …Come to think of it, that was a foolish thing to do.
“So, leave it to Gaelion and the others!”
“Well, if Gaelion-chan says so… I guess it’ll be okay? What if we accidentally provoke the Spirit Tortoise into reviving, and the remaining Takt forces take advantage of the situation?”
“Hmm… That’s exactly why I want Naofumi and the others to get stronger. Gaelion should be able to hold off something like the Spirit Tortoise, so if the worst happens, I’d like them to come to our aid.”
“Hmm…”
My father is grumbling as if he’s troubled.
“Naofumi, do you think Gaelion is unreliable?”
It feels like my Rival is seizing this opportunity to show off!
“It’s not exactly that, but…”
“Father! If anything happens, I’ll take care of it with ease!”
I won’t lose this time. Even if the Spirit Tortoise’s seal is broken and the Phoenix’s seal is broken, I’ll handle it swiftly this time.
“That’s right. In terms of combat power, as long as we have the Spear Hero, they’re no problem. Naofumi, I want you to be extra careful, though.”
He brushed it off casually. I get the feeling my Rival’s evasion skills have improved. The Rival from before would have argued back, but… I’ll have to be on my guard against this one.
“……I get it. But don’t take any unnecessary risks, okay?”
“Of course. When I think about how many lives could be lost because of a Gaelion mistake, I simply can’t afford to fail.”
And so, Rival has decided to lead a diplomatic mission to the country where the Spirit Tortoise is sealed. Not only the Queen, but the people of Siltvelt are going as well. Conversely, for once, my Father and I are taking a different course of action.
“……”
My Assistant just sat there, staring intently at our exchange. Anyway, after discussing various other matters, the meeting seems to have concluded.
It appears my Rival, the Queen, and the representatives from Siltvelt discussed the supplies and funds each country could allocate. It was all technical talk—a real hassle. For the most part, it seems we’re starting to break down the strongholds of the nobles who’ve amassed wealth thanks to our Rival’s rising approval ratings. While Shieldfreeden’s debt is enormous, things seem to be finally starting to turn around. All that’s left is to root out the remaining Takt forces and track down and confiscate the stolen national budget!
So, my Father and I—though we’re not exactly thrilled about it—are here to keep an eye on Ren, who’s likely coming to Cal Mira Island at Rival’s suggestion. Since the portals on Cal Mira Island are out of commission during this time of year, we should at least be able to secure an opportunity to talk with Ren. Ren doesn’t harbor any hostility toward us, so it should be fine even if we run into him.
“Well then, Father, I’m going to go procure some of Filolial-sama’s eggs.”
“So that’s how it’s going to turn out, after all… Well, I’ll be making preparations for departure over in Siltvelt, so please don’t go overboard, Motoyasu-kun. After all, there are so many Filolials, and managing them is a real hassle.”
“Of course! First… let’s stop by and say hello to that Filolial breeder! I’ll bring Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan along!”
Come to think of it, even though we’d bought some from them in this loop, we hadn’t gone to say hello. It’s time to show off Yuki-chan and the others, who’ve grown into legendary Filolials! So, I called out to Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan, and we immediately used a portal to head over to the Filolial producer’s place.
---
“So we’re going to the place where Lord Motoyasu first acquired Yuki and the others, aren’t we?”
“That’s right.”
Before we set off, Yuki-chan asked me that, so I answered. It’s sort of like their birthplace. That breeder runs a great ranch.
“Hmm?”
“The place where you were when you were an egg?”
Sakura-chan and Kou don’t seem to get it.
“By the way, he’s a breeder who’s really dedicated to the Filolial Race. I think he’ll be someone Yuki-chan finds particularly interesting.”
“…I’m looking forward to it.”
Well, I already know he’ll end up causing trouble in the future world, so it’s pretty much stuck in my head. If I told them right now that Yuki is the ranch owner who’s been the talk of Shieldfreeden, I guarantee they’d be shocked.
“Alright, let’s go!”
“Ooh!”
We used a portal to teleport to Filolial Ranch. But what awaited us there was a sight beyond imagination.
“W-what is this—”
“W-what on earth is going on?! Filolial-samaaaaaaaaaaa!”
That’s right—all I could do was scream. The reason was that Filolial’s ranch area had been reduced to a scorched wasteland. The cozy, peaceful atmosphere of the ranch was gone… It had been reduced to scorched earth, with charred fences… and houses… Not a trace of tranquility remained in the area. Yuki-chan examines the charred fence.
“…It seems like this happened quite a while ago.”
I check it out too. Indeed… it’s completely cold to the touch. You can tell at a glance that it wasn’t burning just a moment ago. There’s no sign of smoke either. It looks like a complete ruin.
“W-what on earth is going on!?”
At least, nothing like this has ever happened in any of the loops so far. Could a Filolial producer have caused a fire by being careless with fire?
I’ll search the area. I check not only the Filolial shed where the producers were, but also the site of the warehouse where eggs and such were stored—but all that remains are the charred ruins. Hmm… I suppose I should ask around.
With that in mind, I’ll look for buildings nearby that seem to be associated with the Filolial industry. But… I’ve… found something.
Countless makeshift graves. And… the Monster Merchant and his companions, looking deeply sorrowful as they perform the burials. Yuki-chan and the others have sensed something ominous and are keeping their distance. I’ll have to ask them myself.
“Oh my, I believe that’s the Spear Hero over there. Yes.”
“H-hey, it’s been a while.”
“Yes… Thank you very much for patronizing our shop back then.”
“By the way, what are you doing here?”
“Well… we stopped by here to purchase monster eggs as part of our side business… but unfortunately, we’re not sure exactly what led to this situation. Yes.”
The monster merchant continues his explanation, seeming to struggle with the words.
“This entire area—whether it was bandits or monsters… we’re not sure exactly who—has been reduced to a scorched wasteland by an attack… and since the monsters’ corpses were left lying around, we’re in the middle of burying them.”
…… It seems the monster merchant is simply doing his job as a monster merchant. Since we ran into him in the middle of it, he’s burying the dead monsters. But… normally, monsters shouldn’t have a problem being left out in the open. So why does he have to bury them, I wonder?

Even I, with tears streaming down my face, could see the ominous clouds hanging over that spot, despite it being broad daylight. Beneath those clouds… I could make out a figure that looked like Filolial-sama.

This must be—! It seems that while we were buying time, Zou and Kou must have discovered something. They’ve apparently cleared a wide escape route.
“Oink!? Oo-oo-oo!”
“W-who are you! To dare interrupt our entertainment!”
The Trash and the pig are yelling toward the sound, clearly seething with rage. Soon, from a spot slightly off to the side of where the sound came from… the door to the room was smashed open.
“Oink!?”
“Who’s that!?”
“Huh? Shield Heroes and Spear Heroes, how’s it going?”
At that moment, Panda called out to us. Wait a minute—weren’t you supposed to have gone with Sakura-chan to rescue your Finacée?
“Naofumi! Are you okay?”
It looks like Sakura-chan is here, too. Just then, the dust cloud cleared. I turned my gaze toward Panda, Sakura-chan, and the others.
There, Panda, Éclair, and Sakura-chan were standing with the Queen, her Finacée, and the Tiger Guys.

num: 925
title: Special Edition: I Reincarnated as the Villainous Princess of *The Shield Hero*—What Do You Think I Should Do?
date: 2019/04/01 10:00
url: https://ncode.syosetu.com/n3009bk/925
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
When I came to, I found myself alone in a luxurious room. Where… on earth… am I? Unable to make sense of the situation, I looked at the vanity nearby.
But what I saw there wasn’t my own familiar face… no. This face was unmistakably that of the villain known as Vitch—the root of all this trouble.
Vaguely, I recall a past life…?　I should have been working as an office lady in modern society.
My name was… what was it again? I can’t quite remember. However, there’s no doubt that the woman reflected in this mirror is the foolish and utterly wicked princess who appears as an enemy in *The Rise of the Shield Hero* and *The Spear Hero’s Redo*.
*The Rise of the Shield Hero*. A work that began as a serialization on the “Let’s Become Novelists” website, was later published in book form, and even adapted into an anime.
It’s the story of Naofumi Iwatani, a college student who came to the library to read, and who, while reading a book titled *The Book of the Four Holy Weapons* that he happened to find, is summoned to another world as the Shield Hero—the hero who saves the world depicted within the book. From this clichéd beginning, he becomes entangled in various conspiracies.
Starting with the other three Heroes—who can’t seem to shake their “video game” mentality—the story follows Naofumi as he fends off conspiracies and false accusations orchestrated by Melromarc, the summoning nation that seeks to persecute him because, from a religious perspective, he is the Shield Hero of an enemy nation. I’ve been reading this series since I was in high school. It’s a work that divides readers—some see it as unconventional yet classic, while others view it as classic yet unconventional—and many find it stressful to read.
After *The Rise of the Shield Hero* concluded, the author wrote a new side story titled *The Spear Hero’s Redo*. This story begins with the Spear Hero—who was portrayed as the main antagonist in *The Rise of the Shield Hero*—getting trapped in a loop in a parallel world. Even though he knows the future, the clumsy Spear Hero—whose personality has changed—tries his best to achieve his ideal future… well, not exactly.
It’s a story about him being infatuated with Filo, one of the heroines from *The Rising of the Shield Hero*, while regretting his past mistakes, struggling to help the Shield Hero, and doing his best to meet Filo. Since the Spear Hero—who’s pretty out there in his own way—tries to force his way through necessary steps, this story reveals events that couldn’t be fully depicted in the main series, *The Rising of the Shield Hero*.
I remember this well because I used to read and enjoy both of these stories a lot. I pored over the characters depicted in the novel’s illustrations and across various media. That’s exactly why there’s no way I could mistake her.
This woman—whose features could almost be called those of a beautiful girl when she puts on a innocent facade, but whose face, when she smiles defiantly, can only be described as that of a villain—is undoubtedly… the villainous princess who would later be known as Vitch. Why is she… that villainous princess?
I gaze at the mirror once more. Hmm, she really is a beauty. When she’s not making that villainous expression and just acting naturally… she doesn’t look entirely out of place as the heroine of a manga aimed at men… How does this even work? At the very least, I don’t think it’s the kind of face that gives her away as a villain at first glance. Well, maybe that’s necessary so the events in the original story make sense.
As I thought that, I looked out the window… and caught a glimpse of someone coming up the stairs. That’s… yeah, no doubt about it. It’s the Four Holy Heroes. I quietly opened the door and called out to the soldier on patrol.
“Excuse me.”
“Ha! What may I do for you, Lady Malty?”
The soldier, startled by my voice, saluted while trying to hide his fear. It seems I still hold some power here. Let’s confirm that, just to be safe.
“Could you tell me what’s happening in the castle right now?”
“Ha! Word has spread throughout the castle that, under the orders of the Three Heroes Church and Aultcray King, the Four Holy Heroes have been successfully summoned! Would you like to attend the audience?”
Just as I thought… it seems I’ve really ended up in another world—the world of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*. In fact, there’s even an option to bring up my status icon right in my field of vision…
“No, but… I plan to observe the situation from the back.”
If I recall correctly… the story went that this princess was actually hiding in the back of the throne room.
“I’m sorry for stopping you. Please return to your duties.”
“Ha!”
The soldier saluted and quickly left the scene. He’s probably talking behind my back right now. Well… to be honest, I’ve read quite a bit of the *Shield Hero* series, and it’s one of my favorite works.
It really fuels my ship-related fantasies, and I’m a big fan of the Faubrey arc featuring the Spear Hero… There’s no doubt I’m that kind of person.
My favorite pairing is Spear × Shield. The other way around is good too. I want to see these two interact.
My mind is racing enough that I’d like to take advantage of this opportunity to pull off all sorts of underhanded schemes… but at the same time, my situation in the *Shield Hero* series is extremely dire. After all, in this series, those who retain memories of their past lives are called “reincarnates,” and I was a pawn of the mastermind behind all the chaos that’s wreaking havoc on the world. So… if I make a wrong move, not only will I be killed, but my very soul might be erased.
Suddenly, I pinch my cheek to see if this is a dream, and a sharp pain shoots through me. Yeah… I really have been reincarnated as Vitch. No… I’ve been possessed by her, actually. This Vitch has all sorts of backstory—or rather, she’s a troublesome presence—and if I’ve been possessed by her, there must be all sorts of complications with her original self… but there’s no strange voice or anything.
…How am I going to survive from here on out? The world is experiencing a phenomenon known as “waves.” If we respond too casually to this crisis, not only will the country continue to fall into ruin, but the world itself might be destroyed. After all, the country is secretly stirring up discord among the Heroes, and it seems this country’s religion believes that after framing and killing the Shield Hero, the world will be saved by the Three Heroes.
Only followers of their own religion will be spared from the time of destruction. A new era will begin with the believers and Heroes who have overcome the crisis. When I look up the religious texts and teachings from the world of my past life, I find quite a few descriptions like that. I can imagine it’s a way to keep believers loyal, but the Three Heroes Church has actually put it into practice.
It may seem foolish, but apocalyptic theories are everywhere. I’m sure they existed in the world of my past life, too.
So, given this situation… what should I do?
Should I, as a “good guy” reincarnate, explain the situation to the heroes and try to get them to believe me? Something like, “I know everything about this story, so please trust me.” But… the moment I say that, if a bomb set by the mastermind behind the scenes were to explode, blowing my head to pieces and even obliterating my soul, that would be the end of the story.
Should I decide to be a bystander, do nothing, and keep my distance from the heroes? That’s not a bad option either. At the very least, if I do nothing, I might be able to avoid putting my own life in danger.
But… if I try anything strange… well. If I use my modern knowledge to do something unnecessary, it seems like ruin is bound to be my fate. There’s no doubt this is the kind of story world where getting too cocky will lead to nothing good.
It’s a bit of a meta way of thinking, though. Neither the Queen nor Princess Melty would complain if I just did nothing.
But… if I remember correctly, wasn’t the plot supposed to go something like this: I’d be made to take responsibility for the Hero’s summoning, and the Queen would end up proposing a marriage alliance with that sadistic King Faubrey…? The Queen is compassionate and wants to avoid marrying me off, but if King Faubrey makes a strong demand, there’s a non-zero chance she won’t be able to refuse and will end up offering me to him. It’s easy to imagine that the fact I was a companion of the Spear Hero was one of the reasons she was able to refuse the marriage proposal in the first place.
Taking action is dangerous; doing nothing is dangerous… Hmm. I need to strike a balance… while making sure the Queen doesn’t marry me off, and without provoking the Heroes… Escaping as a commoner or fleeing the country is probably out of the question—it’d be the work of the Shadow Organization or some covert unit. If I tried something like that, they’d suspect I’m up to something and might go ahead with the marriage anyway.
…It’s starting to feel like I’m in a pretty tight spot. Why did I have to end up as Vitch of all people? If I had to choose, I’d have preferred to be Melty or Raphtalia.
No, actually, maybe a background character—like Keel… or maybe someone low-key like Imiya would be better in this situation? But come to think of it, I’m pretty sure even those characters had pretty tragic pasts and circumstances. I don’t want to end up in a situation like that.
……It’s almost like I’m wondering, “Who would actually be a good choice?”…… that’s when it hit me. Elena, the Lazy Pig! If she manages to worm her way into the Hero’s good graces and just keeps an eye on his mood, she’ll be able to slip away safely. She doesn’t even have a particularly tragic backstory.
Or maybe Filo…? No, that’s a bit too much. Just think about it. If I, a modern-day office worker, were to go around saying, “Filo’s name is Filo!”—that would be problematic in so many ways. Besides, I don’t even know if I could reincarnate as a Filolial in the first place.
It would’ve been better if I’d been a mob Filolial raised by the Spear Hero! Long live reincarnation as a monster!
I unconsciously bit my nails, my teeth grinding. I looked every bit the villainess. With that, I quietly made my way to the audience chamber to peek in on the heroes’ audience.
I have a vague grasp of the castle’s layout from my memories as a princess, so I don’t get lost. I wonder how I should go about this? Since all sorts of people from other worlds have come to this one, it should be hard to make money or gain recognition using modern knowledge.
---
Just as I was thinking that, it suddenly—an idea occurred to me.
---
……Is this world I’ve been reincarnated into *The Rise of the Shield Hero*?
Or is it *The Spear Hero’s Second Chance*?
---
If it’s the former, there are still plenty of possibilities waiting to be tapped. If I stay devotedly by the side of Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, especially regarding the king’s and the kingdom’s behind-the-scenes schemes, there’s a high chance things will work out.
It’ll be hard work, but the rewards will be great. The queen will appreciate me, so I can avoid being forced into marriage. The Shield Hero, whose personality hasn’t changed, seems to have a bit of an ulterior motive, but he comes across as a perfectly ordinary young man. He’s the kind of otaku who’ll understand if you just talk to him. He’ll believe me even if I hide my true feelings.
If I nurture him properly… yeah. There’s a high chance we’ll survive. As for the shadowy schemes behind the scenes, let’s leave that to the Queen to handle.
As for self-defense, as long as he has knowledge of the series, he’ll be fine. Since I’ve studied the backstory of *The Spear Hero* thoroughly, I’m sure we’ll manage somehow. Besides, there’s a suspicion that *The Shield Hero* comes from the world of a cooking manga, so I’m a little curious just how delicious his food is.
But… if it turns out to be *The Spear Hero* instead, that would be the worst-case scenario.
After all, in the *Spear Hero* reboot, the protagonist—the Spear Hero—basically can’t tell the difference between a woman’s voice and a pig’s squeal. What’s more, I’m considered the absolute worst pig of them all and am even called the “Crimson Swine.” To top it off, there’s a high chance he’ll try to kill me at the first opportunity.
You know… it feels like he’d just suddenly kill me out of the blue. Even if I’m not doing anything in particular, I could just be walking through the castle when suddenly, out of nowhere, a spear pierces my chest from behind and I die… that’s right, hahahaha… BAD END… that’s totally a possibility. It’s like there’s a 1% chance of a death roll every time I take an action, with no save function.
What do you call that? Like that guy in armor.
It’s a bit of a meta thought, but it seems plausible. It’s the kind of development where something happens in future chapters I haven’t read yet.
That’s because *True Spear*, the sequel to *The Spear Hero’s Redo*, hasn’t been completed yet. There might still be countless unexplored parts or landmines lying around.
Anyway… let’s first confirm which one it is. Judging by what happened earlier, he’ll definitely introduce himself during the audience. I quietly slip behind the throne room and prick up my ears.
“I am the king of this realm, Aultcray Melromarc the 32nd. Heroes, raise your heads!”
Ah, so this is the father of this body—the man who would later be called the “Trash King.” He was the “Hero of the Staff” and known as the “Wise King of Wisdom,” and apparently played a significant role in Melromarc’s past.
Nowadays, though… to put it mildly, he’s a “Madao.” He’s just a hopeless old man—or “Madao,” for short. He’s a troublesome old geezer who won’t come to his senses until he loses a few things. I think he’ll listen to me, his daughter, but when it comes to Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, there’s a high chance he’ll go off the rails. I hope he’ll stop just because I told him to… but since he didn’t seem to back down even after Melty tried to persuade him, it might be difficult.
As I was thinking about this, the king and his entourage began explaining the crisis facing this world.
“I get the gist. So, you’re asking us—who were summoned here—to work for free?”
“That’s a pretty convenient story, isn’t it?”
“We don’t owe you anything, do we? It’d be unbearable to work for free only to be told ‘goodbye’ once peace is restored. Actually, I want to know if there’s even a way for us to get back home—what’s the deal with that?”
“Guh…”

“We’ve also prepared financial aid. We truly want you, the Heroes, to protect the world, and we intend to provide a place for you to do so.”
“Don’t think you can keep us on a leash. We’ll cooperate as long as you don’t become our enemies.”

“Exactly.”
…… Yeah. This flow is definitely *The Shield Hero*. Good, good.
No… I’m starting to feel a little uneasy. If you ask me if I remember the details, I’m a bit iffy on this part of the exchange. But in terms of the flow… it’s definitely right, I think. I listen to the heroes’ self-introductions with my hands clasped together, as if in prayer.
“My name is Ren Amaki. I’m 16 years old and a high school student.”
Yeah, he’s got that shota vibe and is pretty cute. I think he’ll end up having the best personality. He’s the classic hero, isn’t he? Though the events after peace is restored do evoke a lot of sympathy.
But more importantly, what’s coming next!
Shield, shield, shield!

It was a spear-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------! I leaned against the wall, unable to help but feel despair at the death flags that were bound to appear from here on out.
What’s going to happen to my life—!?

*The Rise of the Shield Hero*. It’s a work posted on the “Let’s Become a Novelist” website—which I often browse on my phone during my commute—and it even got adapted into an anime. It’s an adventure story about a protagonist named Naofumi Iwatani, who was reading a book in the library and was summoned as the Shield Hero depicted in the *Book of the Four Holy Weapons*. While getting summoned was a good thing, he ends up enduring all sorts of terrible ordeals from the very beginning, but uses his frustration as fuel to fight back against the injustices he faces. It’s also a story set in a world teeming with enemies—from the other three heroes, who rejoiced at being summoned into a game world but then conspire against and persecute him simply because he’s the Shield Hero, to a religious cult that seeks to torment him.
I’ve been following the series since pretty early on, getting angry at the unfair situations at times, feeling sad at others, and taking joy in seeing the protagonist overcome those injustices and defeat the villains. Some say it’s a revenge story, while others say it’s a rags-to-riches tale. Personally, what made me laugh was an acquaintance who mocked the story, saying something like, “You die just from reading a book and get reincarnated?” When I pointed out that getting summoned while reading a book is actually a pretty old trope in fantasy, he turned bright red and snapped back at me. In any case, there’s no doubt this is a work that divides opinion.
So… wasn’t *The Rising of the Shield Hero* the series that ran daily for a full year before wrapping up? A while after that, following a side story, the spin-off *The Spear Hero’s Redo* began. It’s the story of the Spear Hero—who was originally just a foil—who, after realizing he’d been deceived by that awful woman Bitch, whom he’d trusted, and falling into a slump, gets encouraged by Filo, the mascot and heroine, and goes on a rampage, eventually becoming the protagonist himself.
It started as a side story posted as an April Fools’ joke but became an official spin-off. The story begins with the Spear Hero, Motoyasu Kitamura, having been defeated by the final boss of *The Shield Hero* and sent into a parallel world where he’s stuck in a loop—but this time, he starts the story in his powerful pre-loop state. Personally, I think this one has a lighter tone and is easier to read. In *The Spear Hero*, the protagonist goes to great lengths to help Naofumi Iwatani—the main character of the main series—and reunite with a girl named Filo.
Anyway… it seems I’ve… reincarnated as a character named Takt, the villain who rose to power in *The Shield Hero*. I’ve reincarnated into a character who’s supposed to be a “reincarnated person”—so what the heck am I, exactly? Some jerk with a bad personality reincarnated into Takt, and then I reincarnated into that same Takt… the very concept of “reincarnation” is starting to make no sense at all. I should stop thinking about this.
Well, I don’t exactly pride myself on being quick to switch gears… but yeah. I should probably think this through a bit. Um… oh, the time until the wave arrives is displayed. I guess I just need to do various things, like strengthening myself, within that time frame.
But you know… Takt is the Whip Hero, but since he’s not the official wielder, he can’t really bring out the weapon’s full potential at all. He’s a foolish guy whose only tactic is brute force relying on his high level, and his end isn’t exactly a pretty one. Seriously… if this is true, there’s nothing but despair. Anyway, I need to check things out first. The vague memories of being Takt that keep popping into my head are too hazy to make sense of. Maybe if I react to something, I’ll be able to remember.
With that in mind, I left the room and walked through the mansion. Then, a beautiful girl in a maid’s uniform noticed me and called out.
“Takt, is something wrong?”
“No, just taking a little walk.”
"Right. Then I'll go with you."
Um… oh, I think I get it. This maid is a girl named Ellie who works for Takt. Huh… she's actually pretty cute. Oh? Her background is coming back to me, too.
As a child, she was the daughter of a local noble… a strong-willed, obnoxious brat with Trash parents… She secretly worked to expose her family’s crimes, leading to their downfall, then won them over by showing a compassionate side and trained them… I’ve even heard she used her power to kill a child from the local territory right from the start. Even in a medieval-style world, she’s a pretty brutal, rotten-blooded girl, isn’t she? I can’t believe they made someone like this the heroine!
Plus, she’s just one of many heroines, she doesn’t feel the slightest guilt about her misdeeds, and she’s got this “Leave the scheming to me” attitude. Still, she’s absolutely loyal—not to me, but to Takt. Lately, though, she’s starting to get bored with him and is asserting herself more, so we’re just going through the motions… I know Takt is a lowlife himself, but no matter how cute she is, my “pretty girl sensor” doesn’t register a single reaction to her. I mean, she’s the “True Spear Hero” who yells things like “Buhito!”
Still… I’d be in trouble if she got suspicious. We’re together all the time, so if she realized I’m not who I seem to be and killed me, that’d be the end of me. Is it too risky to turn her down right now?
“Ah, well… I’d rather not deal with the crowds today. How about just the two of us, Ellie? Let’s go for a walk.”
I said this, trying to act as much like Takt as possible. Ellie blushed and nodded, looking a little shy.
“Takt… I understand. Everyone’s over there, so let’s go out the back.”
“Yeah.”
So, with Ellie leading the way, I slipped out of the mansion… and started walking toward the town of Faubrey. I have the map memorized. It’s a big help that I know the layout so well.
From there, I walked with Ellie through the streets of this otherworldly town, trying to keep things as natural as possible… but then Ellie wrapped her arm around mine. Hmm… her chest is pressing against me, and at this angle, she’s touching my… sensitive area too. Hey, Takt, do you always walk like this with girls?! That’s gross! Even if you’re a womanizer, you should at least think about how you look to others!
“Where are we going?”
“How about the shooting range? Let’s take care of those guys we caught. You said you wanted to blow off some steam, didn’t you?”
…Why can’t you come up with anything but such gory suggestions? I know that “taking care of those guys we caught” at the shooting range isn’t a normal thing to do, no matter how you look at it. Plus, judging by the flow of the conversation, this seems like something she does on a regular basis. I don’t want a heroine who does stuff like that all the time… No, does Takt really not realize this? Well, since she’s an antagonist in *The Shield Hero*, maybe her character is just exaggerated to the extreme. I hope that’s the case. Or else it just means Takt is that much of a scumbag.
“I’m not in the mood for that right now. Maybe we should go grocery shopping or something.”
“Really? What should we buy…? How about we kill a fresh Filolial from the market and make some fried chicken?　It tastes better if you make them suffer a lot before killing them, doesn’t it?”
Filolials are bird-like monsters in this world that pull carriages, and characters like Filo—the heroine of *The Shield Hero*—belong to that species. I’ve heard some are eaten, but… uh, this is bad. Just hearing “Filolial cuisine” makes me think of *The Spear Hero*. “Making them suffer first”? If this were a spin-off, they’d be killed in a way even worse than when their eggs were cracked.
…I’ve completely lost my appetite. I don’t want to die, so I can’t eat a Filolial. Absolutely not.
But what the hell is up with these guys? They’re even worse than how they’re portrayed in *The Shield Hero* series. Just because they’re enemy characters doesn’t mean they should torture a living creature before strangling it—what kind of mindset do they have?
“Come to think of it…”
Even if it feels unnatural, I’d better take the lead in this conversation or things might get ugly. No, wait—Takt is a pretty whimsical guy, so even if I say something weird out of the blue, he might accept it to some extent. After all, he suddenly started talking about a “slow life” and bought a deserted island to develop, and he’s been making “corporate slave drinks” in Shieldfreeden under the guise of “domestic policy cheats.”
“So, these ‘waves’ have started happening—but were the Legendary Four Holy Heroes actually summoned?”
“I heard that pig and the folks from other countries are holding a meeting to summon them, right? Aren’t they still in the middle of planning the ritual? I thought they were currently gathering representatives from each country.”
Ah… If I recall correctly, according to the backstory of *The Rising of the Shield Hero*, Faubrey was supposed to be leading the effort to summon them. But in the middle of that, Melromarc beats them to it and performs the summoning. That fact doesn’t become widely known until a little later. Since Ellie should be answering my question based on what she knows, the timing must be before the Heroes are summoned… right? Yeah, that’s the early part of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*.
At that thought, a chill ran down my spine, and a cold sweat broke out.
Is the world I’m in right now the world of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*? Or is it the world of *The Spear Hero’s Redo*? No… it might actually be the world of *The True Spear Hero’s Redo*.
If it’s *The Rise of the Shield Hero*, that’s still better. Takt just ends up getting his comeuppance in the end, and since I’ve read the original work, there might be ways for me to survive by defusing various foreshadowing flags… maybe.
At the very least, I want to cut ties with the members of Takt’s harem. Not a single one of them has a decent background or personality. After all, we’ve seen plenty of that in *The Spear Hero* and *The True Spear Hero*. To be blunt, even in Takt’s current memories, these women are so deranged that it’s presumptuous to even call them heroines. They’re the kind of people who, in high-pitched voices, suggest they want to watch people get killed or see guts splatter everywhere. If you have even a shred of sanity, you’d want to keep your distance from them. I don’t even want to think about the fact that people like this are living normal lives and blending into the world. That’s why Takt thinks this:
“Since I was reincarnated, the world has been gradually getting better.”
You’ve got to be kidding me. It’s just convenient for you, isn’t it?
Still… it’s true that they’re a nuisance because they’re in a position to fully leverage Takt’s background and authority… I’ll have to handle them skillfully, though. What I have to be careful about is that if the Four Holy Heroes find out I’m a reincarnated person and expose the mastermind or my true circumstances, it’ll be dangerous. It seems some kind of “bomb” like that has been planted on reincarnated people, and several have died in the story. The fact that something similar has been planted on Takt… should have been revealed in the book version.
However, since Takt already holds that position… there’s still a way out if I cooperate with the Heroes without revealing the inside story—just making it look like I’m cooperating even though I can’t actually tell them the truth. It’s like this… I’ll just send that worthless woman the Heroes seem likely to beat, and have them take them out one by one. You know, the one who’s like the weakest of the Four Heavenly Kings… or something like that.
Wait, hold on!
This is a pretty underhanded plan. Let’s not do it. It’s totally in line with Takt’s nature. You shouldn’t let your memories blend into my personality.
I guess this is something I’ll have to handle myself… for the sake of the world. Maybe I should fight a strong opponent to weaken their forces or something… It’d be great if he’d reform, but he doesn’t seem like the type. If I go with the “Let’s cooperate with the Heroes!” approach, I feel like I’d end up running amok at the worst possible moment—or slip up and end up as enemies anyway.
For now, I should probably stop thinking about this scenario based on the premise that it’s *The Rising of the Shield Hero*. Instead, let’s consider the case where it’s a redo of *The Spear Hero* or *The True Spear Hero*.
That’s the worst-case scenario. The Spear Hero is far stronger than me right from the start of the loop. Even if I mobilized all the women, I wouldn’t stand a chance. He’s a monster I absolutely cannot defeat in a straightforward fight. To win, I’d have to be truly recognized by this Sacred Weapon I’m holding.
But… as I am now, no matter what I do, the Whip isn’t accepting the enhancements based on my knowledge of the original story. Seriously, the enhancements just aren’t working… I’ve gotten a little stronger, but… it’s painfully obvious that I can’t enhance it properly. So this is what it means to not be recognized by a weapon…
Early on in the “Spear Hero’s Redo,” since Motoyasu Kitamura’s memories of Takt are vague, if I try to get along with him before we become enemies… and become friends with the “Shield Hero,” there’s a high chance he’ll listen to me. But… after that, it’s the worst-case scenario. He’ll undoubtedly use every trick in the book to eliminate Takt.
That said… up until the Melromarc arc, it’s still possible—just barely—to establish a cooperative relationship with Naofumi through discussion. However, if it’s after that, the Faubrey Pig King will rat him out for cheating, and he’ll be stripped of his weapon and executed. He’ll be dealt with in a single sentence. And if he’s the True Spear Hero… that’s bad. Really bad.
Just like in some mystery story, you’d be forced to endure a terrifying ordeal on a deserted island! Even if you know who the culprit is, you can’t do anything about it—what kind of hell is that?! Monsters straight out of a splatter horror movie would come after you. “Can you survive?” Of course not! It’s total annihilation!
Even if you somehow managed to avoid that… there’s no doubt the Spear Hero would come out of hiding and do everything in his power to hunt me down. Being targeted by a killer I absolutely can’t beat is the absolute worst! The best thing to do is ditch this weapon, change my face, hair color, and name, and make a clean getaway! It’d be great if I could switch bodies using a homunculus or something…
But… even if I tried something like that… there’s a high chance the women from the harem would come after me.
Why did I have to end up as Takt, of all things! Well, I guess it might be better than becoming Bitch, aka the Crimson Swine. That guy’s got a death sentence hanging over his head. If I’m going to become something anyway… assuming I can’t be one of the Heroes… since I’m a guy, I’d rather be the old man who runs the weapon shop!
All I’d have to do is be nice to the Shield Hero, and if I work as a blacksmith, I’d probably manage just fine, right? I’ve been reading books where all sorts of mysteries are being revealed. Whether it’s a shield or a spear, it’s a position where I could get by reasonably well. If I were a girl, would Elena be the safest bet? It’d be nice to be raised as a Filolial Spear Hero while being a background character. Just being around him would get me by to some extent. I’d just have to go on saying “Filololon” or something, right?
But… in this world, we don’t see any reincarnated monsters, do we…? Given the typical pattern of the posting sites where this is published, it wouldn’t be strange if they existed. Yet, as things stand, there aren’t any. It feels like there might be some hidden backstory. It’s the kind of series where discarded concepts and such get revealed, after all… At most, there’s only that one girl, but she’s an ally. To begin with, given the nature of the hosting site, I don’t think it’s treated as a “monster reincarnation” story.
Anyway… what matters is whether it’s a shield, a spear, or a True Spear. Can’t I get to Melromarc with a weapon like a whip…? At worst, if I can stop the summoning, my chances of survival will skyrocket.
Damn… nothing! The closest option is probably Zeltoble. Even then, it’ll take a few days. But if I went by plane or something, I’d stand out too much. Besides, this world wasn’t really suited for airplanes to begin with. …There’s a way to figure out whether it’s a shield or a spear right here.
“Takt, where are you going?”
After finishing our walk and grocery run and dropping Ellie off at the mansion, I turned my back and started walking away.
“Just running an errand at the castle. Don’t follow me. I don’t really like it when people are too clingy, you know?”
If I don’t reject her with this brusque attitude, she’ll definitely follow me. Still, just to be safe, I decided to activate a cloaking-like skill—called “Cloking”—that was inside my whip to shake off any pursuers. Ugh… I can’t use this for very long. Even though that “Spear Hero” guy uses it all the time.
Combined with my magic… it’d be easier to just use magic normally… but I can only cast up to “Drifa.” I’m not exactly sure what Takt’s magical affinity is, but I should be able to use fire magic, so I’ll manage. Anyway, I managed to shake off any potential pursuers and made it to the castle.
“Hey.”
“Well, well, Lord Takt. What brings you here today?”
I called out to the receptionist at the castle. This time… it looks like a soldier under my influence.
“I’ve got a quick question.”
“What might that be?”
“I’m pretty sure there’s a gathering of leaders from various countries coming up, right? So, do you happen to know where the Queen of Melromarc is right now? Even if it’s just a rumor, tell me anything—no matter how small.”
I asked the castle receptionist as naturally as possible, pretending to be thinking of that Bitch.
“Please wait a moment.”
The soldier, as if answering my question, led me deeper into the castle to inquire. I was shown into a private room, so I sat down on a chair for the time being… but that Takt guy—maybe it’s just a habit—was sitting with his legs crossed so arrogantly that even I was surprised. “Sit with a little more class,” I thought to myself, and consciously sat down normally. About ten minutes later… the soldier hurried into the room.
“Excuse me.”
“Ah.”
What is this…? I felt a wave of unbearably unpleasant sweat run down my spine.
“Well… I’ve been instructed to handle this matter as peacefully as possible, but there are conflicting reports that he’s been led away by someone claiming to be the ‘Spear Hero.’ It’s likely a rumor, but since I was told to report even the smallest detail, I’m bringing this to your attention.”
It was the Spear!!! AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH! I’m going to be brutally slaughtered—!
And it’s the later part, right?! No doubt about it! It’s gotta be at least the second half of Zeltoble or later, isn’t it AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!?
I don’t know if it’s one of my many playthroughs or if that guy got stuck in a loop during the early stages of *True: The Spear Hero*, but what the hell is going to happen to me after this, AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!

Guh… Itsuki, damn you! Landing a direct hit on my imagination at a time like this.
