Master-sama got down from the carriage and went to talk with the important-looking people in charge of the place, just like he does with Mel-chan sometimes. Then he came back and it seemed like he was about to explain what they’d do next. Everyone gathered around, waiting for Master-sama’s instructions.
“Ahem… so, we’ve been asked to investigate this dungeon that suddenly appeared. Apparently, once you enter, it gets dark and everyone gets separated—that’s just how the mechanism works—but supposedly you can regroup afterward.”
“I see… that’s a bit worrying.”
“Indeed… Ren, you went in ahead of us. I’d like to hear what you found.”
“Right. Me, Éclair, and Wyndia went in to investigate. What we learned: there are shadow-like monsters inside the dungeon, there are doors partway through that let you escape, and anyone carrying a Legendary Weapon, Seven Star Weapon, or Vassal Weapon has their level and weapon reset upon entry—you can’t change forms again until you find the corresponding weapon inside the dungeon. Once you exit, the reset lifts.”
Um, Filo didn’t really get it, but it sounded like something about not being able to use claws properly anymore?
“Also, apparently for whoever’s carrying the corresponding weapon, any weapon dropped inside changes into that type.”
“So it’s some kind of hero correction thing… And the Dragon Hourglass has decorations we’ve never seen before too… What in the world is this? Also, this system sounds suspiciously familiar—what a mysterious, mystifying maze this is.”
“Maaa~ka~fu~shi~gi~”
“Filo, hush. You’re killing the mood.”
“Ehh…”
It just sounded like such a fun phrase that Filo said it, but Master-sama told her to be quiet.
“In that case, if I can’t fight properly alone, maybe it’s safest for me to just wait here?”
Just as Master-sama muttered that, Atla-chan popped out of his shield.
“Naofumi-sama, information has come through the shield from the labyrinth’s hourglass. It says that Naofumi-sama would be able to clearly see traps within the labyrinth, easily disarm them, and set them up so monsters get caught instead. Also, that he’d be able to reunite with companions quickly.”
“…Didn’t some spirits just make this place for fun or something? If so, I’m going home.”
“I thought the same and questioned them thoroughly, but even the spirits don’t seem to understand it. However… I do have concerns that this may not be a particularly good situation.”
Tch! Master-sama clicked his tongue.
“Either way, it looks like we’ll need to do a proper investigation. Everyone, that’s how it is—we’re all going into the labyrinth together to investigate.”
“Yes. Everyone, let’s go.”
Filo didn’t really get it, but it seemed like she was going into the dungeon together with Master-sama and everyone. As they pushed further and further into the cave, the bright area behind them gave way to darkness ahead. Big Sister was using light magic, and everyone else had their own lanterns too. Then, as they kept going, suddenly everything went pitch black.
“Just like they said, it’s gotten dark. Everyone, make sure to—”
And then Master-sama’s voice just cut off partway through. Right after that, the darkness lifted and it became bright again. Filo could see a cave passage—seemed a bit spacious. The claws she was holding weren’t the ones Mel-chan had taught her—they’d turned back into her very first claws.
“Master-samaaa? Where are youuu?”
Master-sama had been right there just a moment ago, right? They were supposed to get separated but be able to reunite quickly—that’s what they said. Filo sensed someone’s presence behind her. So she turned around.
“Filo-taaan!”
“It’s Spear Guy! Yaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!”
“Please wait, Filo-taaaaan! To think we’d be together right from the start, even though we’re supposed to get separated—this is truly the guiding hand of destiny, I say!”
“Yaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!”
Filo ran with all her might, fleeing Spear Guy for dear life. Along the way she ran into some monsters, but she didn’t have time to worry about them—if she slowed down, Spear Guy would catch up—so she kicked them aside and dashed straight through.
“W-wait—”
“Yaaaaaaaaaaaa!”
Filo kept dashing down through the cave, floor after floor, for as long as it took until Spear Guy’s voice couldn’t be heard anymore. Zoom! Finally, once his voice faded away completely, she breathed a sigh of relief and looked around.
“Where am Iiii?”
Where am I~ Filo’s own voice echoed back at her… Monsters showed up in response to the sound, but Filo took them down easily with a kick. Then, there were some claws lying around, so she went to pick them up, and they got sucked right into her equipped claws. Um, these ones were stronger, so she switched to them. There was also a collar and some clothes lying around, so she picked those up too, planning to give them to Master-sama later.
“Master-samaaa!”
Ugh… where could Master-sama be~? Along the way there was a click sound and she got a little dizzy for a moment, felt kind of sick, got blown into a wall by a sudden gust of wind—Filo was getting sick of this! She wanted to see Master-sama soon! So Filo pushed on, determined. She was looking for the exit Sword Guy had mentioned. Surely Master-sama would find the exit and come out too. And as she kept moving forward…
“Sniff sniff… ah, I smell a Filolial~”
She didn’t know whose scent it was, but it was definitely a Filolial scent, different from the monsters in this cave. Since they’d said companions could regroup, she figured someone must be up ahead. So Filo headed toward the smell to reunite with them.
Then—she came out into a wide space, similar to the one she’d first been in with Spear Guy, and there was the Filolial the scent belonged to. It was cherry-blossom pink, with white-tipped feathers, and it turned to look at Filo. Ah, its eyes were the same cherry-blossom pink too. Who could it be~? A Filolial she’d never seen before, and just like Filo, it was in Queen form.
“Ah, there’s a Filolial—who are youuu?”
“Filo’s name is Filo!”
“Sakura’s name is Sakura!”
Oh really~? Seemed like this Filolial’s name was Sakura. Was it one that Spear Guy raised? Never seen it in the village before~ But Spear Guy probably raises Filolials elsewhere too, so it wasn’t strange that there’d be Filolials she’d never met.
“Where did Sakura come from~?”
“Um, so~ Sakura came with Naofumi and everyone to investigate the dungeon, and Sakura got separated~”
“Filo came with Master-sama to investigate the dungeon too, and got separated too~”
“Really~?”
Sakura seemed to be saying Master-sama’s name. Someone with the same name? Probably Master-sama, right~? Was this one Master-sama’s Filolial instead of Spear Guy’s? Would this kid recognize Master-sama, she wondered?
“Hey, have we met somewhere before~?”
“Hmm? Filo doesn’t know. Did we meet at the nest in the village~?”
“Hmm? Don’t know about a village~. What about Naofumi’s castle~?”
Master-sama has a castle~? Was it Mel-chan’s castle?
“That claw~”
“Filo’s claw~?”
Sakura was staring at Filo’s claws.
“Looks like the claw Gaelion has~”
“This is Filo’s!”
A dragon having Filo’s claws—no wayyy!
“Really~? Then maybe it’s a different one~?”
Sakura seemed to be a Filolial who didn’t know Filo at all. When Filo turned into human form, Sakura did too. Her build seemed the same as Filo’s.
“Ah, I hear a voice. Hellooo?”
A voice that sounded a lot like Master-sama’s called out. The two of them looked toward the sound, and out of the darkness came… Master-sama…?
“Ah, it’s Naofumi~”
He was carrying the same shield as Master-sama, but he looked like a kinder version of Master-sama? Filo knew that whenever Master-sama made that kind of face, he was thinking of something weird. But Master-sama was tilting his head, looking at Sakura. Is Sakura going to be okay~? When Master-sama gets like that, he ends up dragging Filo and everyone into something strange. Ah, but when he’s in a good mood he pets them too, so maybe it’s not so bad? Lately he’s had that look on his face more often. Mel-chan said she was being too cautious about it.
“Is that… Sakura-chan over there? But she’s so short, and young… about the same as Yuki-chan. Huh? Cherry-blossom colored eyes? No wait, like what Motoyasu-kun mentioned before…”
Hmm? Master-sama just called Spear Guy “-kun”?
“And the one standing next to her is the Filo-chan Motoyasu-kun told me about!? No doubt about it. She’s the spitting image of the picture he showed me before.”
Somehow this one resembled Master-sama, but something was different.
“Yep! Filo’s name is Filo!”
“R-right. But shouldn’t these two be the same person…”
“Maaa~ka~fu~shi~gi~”
“That girl looks like Sakura-chan, but she’s smaller and her eye color is different… it really is strange that a Filo-chan would be here of all places. But if I try to explain this properly and go back, who knows how Motoyasu-kun will react, he gets so scared… hmm…”
“Master-sama, are you trying to introduce Filo to Spear Guy~?”
“No, that’s not it… but according to what Gaelion-chan said, there’s a possibility that Filo-chan and Sakura-chan are actually separate individuals…?”
“Sakura is Sakura~?”
“Ah, yeah. That’s true, but… I’m just wondering what on earth is going on here… Is this labyrinth the cause after all, I wonder?”
Master-sama started muttering to himself, deep in thought.
“Looks like Master-sama but something’s different. So mystifying~ this is kind of fun!”
“Maaa~ka~fu~shi~gi~”
“Maaa~ka~fu~shi~gi~!”
“No, wait, you two are saying that with zero tension, but this isn’t really the kind of situation where you can crack a funny joke, you know?”
And so, Filo ended up reuniting in the dungeon with someone who looked like a kinder version of Master-sama, and with Sakura. For now, it seemed the three of them would be moving forward together.

Sleeping Cat and Waking Bird
=====
That was a memory from a certain day, I say. It was an unremarkable day when Father, back when he was still the first Shield Hero, was tending to the monster stables in the village as part of his usual morning routine. I too was over in the Filolial stables next door, enjoying a refreshing morning.
“Ku… Kue.”
“Kue.”
The Filolial-samas suddenly grew restless, glancing all around, before all turning to face the same direction in unison. I was wondering just what had happened when—
“Naofumi-sama!”
Father had just stepped out of the monster stables when Big Sister’s voice rang out with unusual intensity, so I found myself heading outside as well, over toward where Father and the others were. The whole village was already up and about, looking forward to breakfast, and they too tilted their heads curiously at the sound of Big Sister’s voice as they watched the scene unfold.
“Ah… looks like we’ve got visitors,” Father muttered, sighing slightly, and set off walking beside Big Sister with a tired air about him.
“Ohh? Seems like something’s come up,” said Older Sister, who had apparently just gotten up despite drinking late into the night. She wasn’t even the least bit drunk, which put everyone nearby on edge.
“Is there some kind of problem, I wonder? Shall Motoyasu handle it, I say?”
“Motoyasu, you don’t need to do anything. There’s no real problem, so just behave yourself.”
“Understood, indeed!”
Father seemed to understand something about the situation. Looking for all the world like he was just heading out for a morning stroll, he walked ahead… toward the village entrance. Thud thud thud thud! The Filolial-samas all lined up together near the entrance, and Rival, for whatever reason, was flat on the ground on the other side, prostrating itself. And there, beyond them… stood a rounded, cat-like Demi-Human standing about a hundred and thirty centimeters tall, alongside a bird-type monster with dazzling plumage evoking crimson flames, its long peacock-like tail feathers trailing behind it. Looking more closely at the cat-like Demi-Human, it had a lizard-like tail covered in fur and was wearing overalls. Some traveler passing through the neighboring town, perhaps? From somewhere around Siltvelt? But judging by the reactions of the Filolial-samas, Rival, and Big Sister, that clearly wasn’t the case. Just what in the world was going on, I wondered?
“Rival, what exactly are you doing, I say?”
“Nano, shut up! Rival doesn’t have time to deal with you right now. Be quiet, nano!”
What a strange reaction. Ah! Look, over there’s a big Filolial-sama! It had the appearance of an ordinary Filolial, but it couldn’t fool these Motoyasu eyes, I say! Just as I was about to approach the large Filolial-sama, Kuu, Marine, and Midori stopped me.
“Mokkun, no!”
“I don’t think you should upset that person’s mood!”
“Goshujin-sama, I feel like you really shouldn’t upset that person’s mood.”
Filo-tan also approached Father, pointing at the bird-type monster beside the cat Demi-Human, warning him too.
“You’re seriously making everyone uncomfortable. Maybe tone it down a little, hm?”
“Nah, nah, I’m not putting off that much of a presence over here, am I? Ahh, this is a problem… I’m supposed to be the casual, laid-back type, you know.”
Somehow it felt exactly like royalty had shown up incognito among commoners—the cat Demi-Human and the bird monster seemed at a loss for how to respond, chatting between themselves.
“Ah, first off, everyone, don’t worry, I don’t have such a difficult personality that I’d get upset over something like this, so feel free to relax. If anything, I’m the one intruding here, just a visitor, that’s all.”
The bird monster spread one wing out like a hand, addressing the Filolial-samas reassuringly. At that, the Filolial-samas seemed to relax slightly, some of the tension draining from them.
“Right, right, ease up, everyone. Sorry for the sudden visit without any warning. We happened to run into an old friend nearby and figured we’d drop by to say hello while introductions were being made. Thought at the very least we ought to greet you properly. Oh, and that bird over there apparently just had something really good happen right before this, so it’s in an especially good mood—won’t get mad no matter what you do right now.”
“As long as your soul isn’t rotten, you can do whatever you like!”
The cat Demi-Human pointed at the bird monster, explaining this to Father. Did something happen if your soul was rotten? According to what Father said, apparently there was no one here with a rotten soul.
“And yet, both the dragon and the Filolials are on high alert regardless.”
“Raph…”
Raph-chan, perched on Father’s shoulder, cried out.
“Ah, that’s because of this troublesome bird here. Being the progenitor of all winged creatures, it’s letting off this bizarre aura without holding back at all. Quite the nuisance, isn’t it?”
“Being popular is a hard cross to bear… though you’re one to talk, letting your own presence leak out everywhere.”
“Mine’s fine because only certain beings can even sense it. Otherwise they wouldn’t notice at all.”
“…If you could hide it, you could’ve just taken that thing down yourself. And what’s with the ‘I was alone’ bit, huh?”
In response to Father, the cat Demi-Human answered with an easy, unbothered expression.
“The other side wasn’t stupid enough to fall for that, you know? Well, maybe they were a little stupid. Anyway, I really was alone back then. I’m not lying, and besides, you wouldn’t leave the fate of the world up to just anyone, would you?”
“Yeah, sure…”
The cat Demi-Human clapped its hands together with a small pop, shifting its gaze away from Father toward the rest of us standing behind him.
“Well then, allow me to properly introduce myself. To you all, I suppose I’d be what’s known as a god-hunter. My name is Ark. I had a bit of an encounter with Naofumi-kun here, and I ended up lending him a hand.”
“Yeah, that’s right.”
“Yes, we were saved by you back then.”
The one who had introduced itself as the cat Demi-Human, now revealed to be the god-hunter Ark, spoke thus. And Father and the others nodded along. So then, this was apparently someone Father owed a great deal to, from back when he was working to defeat the Crimson Swine’s true body. Father turned his gaze toward the bird monster standing beside Ark.
“You’ve probably already heard from Ark, but I’m Naofumi Iwatani. This is Raphtalia beside me. There are plenty of others behind us too, but introducing everyone would take forever, so if you want to talk to them later, go ahead.”
“Sure, sure. My name is… well, like him, I go by a lot of names, but I suppose I’m most often called the Phoenix. Not that I’m immortal or anything, mind you.”
“Well, it wouldn’t make much sense for a bunch of god-hunters to be immortal themselves.”
“Exactly. We just sleep and wake up, that’s all.”
“I mean, that’s not really a name though, is it?”
“I know, I know. There’s also ‘Hōō,’ but that already exists in this world too, doesn’t it? So for simplicity’s sake, just call me Hō—might end up being my next name anyway.”
Having said that, the bird monster who called itself Hō gave a small bow.
“Ah, I also happen to have the role of a god-hunter myself, though it’s different from this one here, who brings eternity to an end.”
At the mention of ending eternity, Hō pointed at Ark. So it had a title like that too, huh.
“Sometimes I’m called the progenitor of all winged creatures too, you know. World renewal is technically his… job, but don’t worry. This world isn’t so old or rotten that it needs renewing.”
It all sounded like quite a grand conversation—were these two on the same level as Ren or Black Thunder, I wondered?
“So you, who seems on par with that one, are you like some kind of dragon progenitor? You’ve got that sort of vibe about you.”
Father asked, looking over at Rival, who still had its head lowered. Meaning—this was Rival’s original source! If that were true, then it was an enemy, I say!
“Hmm? No, compared to the progenitor, Ark thinks it’s more like being siblings, actually. The dragons just sort of treat it as a superior out of formality, but it’s a bit different.”
“Sounds pretty similar to me.”
“Hmm… maybe think of it like an in-law relationship? Does that make more sense?”
No blood relation, but a position like the clan chief’s brother-in-law… I see, that did paint a somewhat different picture, I say.
“Haaah…”
Father let out quite a weary sigh.
“Ah, you don’t need to look so troubled about it. It’d be a shame if you served up a plate of bubuzuke to a visitor from another world, wouldn’t it?”
That was clearly code for “please leave already.” Even looking like that, it knew all about Japanese customs!
“Well… Ark understands the anger, the ‘why now, you’re late, you idiots!’ kind of feeling, but there are countless worlds out there, and it’s not like anyone can help it when certain parties were working to keep the alarms from ever going off. Omniscience and omnipotence are nothing but arrogance anyway—full of holes, through and through.”
Ark let out quite the heartfelt complaint.
“While staying here, at the very least, Ark will let you vent your anger at it. You’ve more than earned that right. Still, would you mind hearing out our side, and a bit of a report?”
“What is it?”
“The mastermind behind this whole affair, in the world where they were operating—they’ve been made to pay. There won’t be any more waves stirred up from that direction.”
Ark stated this flatly. Now that I thought about it, this Ark fellow—I couldn’t sense anything from it at all, not even the faintest presence. Was this what being a god-hunter meant, I wondered?
“…I see.”
Father, having listened to the report calmly, let his frown ease somewhat.
“The person in charge tried making all sorts of excuses, but honestly, it was almost laughable that they thought we wouldn’t dig deeper. The whole world had rotted through, completely, on a systemic level. To them, Ark probably looks like nothing short of a slaughterer.”
Well, whatever the case, Ark laughed… though somehow, that smile felt strangely familiar to me.
“Anyway, that’s why we’ll be staying here a while, if that’s alright.”
“Sure, sure. If you two are around, I bet any troublesome types who show up will just get handled on their own. Just don’t slack off, got it?”
“I know, I know. The least we can do is repay a night’s lodging and a meal.”
Hō ordered the Filolial-samas to disperse, and once they’d settled into relaxing however they pleased, it rejoined the conversation. So, meaning, these two god-hunters would be staying in the village for a while. The villagers too dispersed, whispering among themselves in small chats. What should Motoyasu do now, I wondered? Just as I was thinking of heading back to my daily routine with the Filolial-samas, Hō turned to look at me.
“Ah, you—I recognize you. I remember now. You were making news in a world Hō was staying in before coming here, weren’t you? Motoyasu Kitamura, was it?”
“What? You know about Motoyasu?”
“Told you already, didn’t I? Before coming here, in a world Hō was indebted to, Hō remembered a bit about him. Well, needless to say, he’s quite the celebrity there. Whew-hoo, what a ladies’ man! Just like Hō!”
Father was glaring at me. Or rather, glaring at both me and my spear, to be precise. There was a god-hunter standing right nearby, and you didn’t even notice?! And more to the point, is your world full of nothing but idiots like this?! I could practically feel Father thinking exactly that.
“I—I don’t know anything about that, I say!”
“Well, no surprise you don’t remember. Hō wasn’t quite like this back then… there was a lot going on. Now Hō’s shining this brilliantly, though!”
There seemed to be some kind of story behind it. I didn’t know the details of Hō’s circumstances, but this was a relief, honestly. Still, the vibe was a little cringeworthy, I say. Watching it felt uncomfortably like looking at my past self.
“…The news, huh.”
“Yep. The story was that he’d been killed over some romantic entanglement, but he was actually summoned to this world and managed to avoid death… there are still traces of causal interference from the mastermind behind this whole affair. I see, I see. Since he ‘died,’ all sorts of related parties apparently went on a rampage, and the mastermind met quite a gruesome end because of it. At the university… oh wait, that’s getting into privacy territory Hō shouldn’t be discussing. Sorry about that.”
Hō seemed to be talking about something from my original world. Incredibly, deeply irrelevant information, I say.
“Oh? So he tried to avoid his own destruction by making use of his original nature in an emergency, huh. I see, I see. Purely coincidental, but maybe it was some kind of fate that we and you ended up in the same world together.”

Video Crystal Letter
Ren and Itsuki, responding to my summons, came over to my house, I say.
“Huh? Ren, Itsuki, what are you two doing here?”
Even Father showed up. A bit unexpected, but no matter, I say.
“Yeah, apparently Motoyasu called both of us here separately with a message.”
“I came here wondering just what this could be about.”
“Hmm…”
And so, Ren and Itsuki knocked on the door of my house—knock knock.
“…No answer?”
“Honestly, calling people over and then this.”
“Doesn’t seem to be locked, though?”
“Well then, shall we let ourselves in first? Perhaps it’s something urgent.”
Ren and Itsuki went ahead and stepped inside my house. Inside, there was a video crystal I’d placed on the table, along with a note.
“What is this…?”
“Addressed to us. Looks like it says to play the video crystal.”
“Honestly, what is with that man.”
With a tone of exasperation, Itsuki activated the video crystal. A recording appeared, showing me sitting in a chair with Yuki-chan on my lap.
“Wazzzup! Ren, Itsuki, you watching?”
“……”
“……”
Ren and Itsuki’s silent, expressionless stares were quite the sight, I say.
“What is this. Sounds like the kind of line someone says right before a cuckolding reveal. So the homewrecker would be Motoyasu-kun, but then who’s the one being cheated on?”
“Based on the visuals, wouldn’t that be Yuki-san?”
“Yuki’s Motoyasu’s Filolial though. Even so, being a homewrecker suits him disturbingly well.”
“Well, Motoyasu-kun is handsome, after all.”
“Waah, what are you doing, let Kitamura-Kou join too!”
“Kuro too!”
Kou and Kuro-chan burst into the recording, mid-filming. The two of them bounced around, tangling themselves up with me while I sat there with Yuki-chan on my lap.
“And just like that, the cuckold video turned into a home video.”
“Seriously, what is going on here?”
“Makes no sense at all.”
“Hold on, we’re in the middle of filming right now, I say. Just be patient a bit.”
“Yaaay, Naofumi-sama, are you watching?”
Yuki-chan called out Father’s name at that point, being considerate toward the Hero who hadn’t been mentioned yet among the group.
“Why is Yuki-chan saying my name at a moment like this? What exactly does that mean?”
“Doesn’t seem like Yuki-san had any deep meaning behind it.”
“Yeah, no doubt she has no idea what it even means.”
Time to start over, I say. Since re-filming would’ve been a hassle, I just kept rolling as is.
“Now then, the reason I called you two here today is no small matter. There is a certain truth I must reveal to you, indeed. This is a major announcement, I say.”
“What could this possibly be about? Why can’t he just tell us directly, I wonder?”
“Even if he told us directly, he’d probably act like there’s nothing to be scared of.”
“Apparently there is something he fears, though.”
“A woman gone off the deep end, wasn’t it? Not exactly something the two of us could handle.”
The me in the video didn’t bother pausing to consider timing or reply to Father and the others’ conversation. After all, the only audience I’d imagined for this recording was Ren and Itsuki watching it.
“What I have hidden, working in the shadows to reveal to you two the truth of this kingdom… was none other than… the rabbit…”
At that exact moment, I transformed into my Usauni form on screen.
“It is I! Usauni Motoyasu, ribbit! Ren, Itsuki, have you both finally realized just how rotten this kingdom and your companions truly are, ribbit? Thought it was about time to teach you both a lesson, ribbit!”
Bam! I struck a pose. I’d even edited the video crystal to add speed lines for effect.
“Usauni Motoyasu, Shadow Clone Jutsu, I say! Shu-shu-shu-shu!”
With that, the me inside the video crystal showed off an afterimage trick, moving at high speed thanks to my elevated stats.
“……”
“……”
“To all you Heroes out there, if you found this video crystal even the slightest bit entertaining!”
“Don’t forget to subscribe to the channel!”
“It’d make me super happy if you left a like, ribbit!”
With that, I released the clone technique and, noticing Yuki-chan and the others slightly startled by my transformation, signaled them for an outing. Yuki-chan caught on and shifted into her Filolial form.
“Well then, I’ll be heading out for a while, so farewell, ribbit-byeee!”
“Off we go, then!”
“Departure time!”
“Kuro-chan, keep this a secret from Ren, alright, I say?”
“Got it! Shadow Saint Hero’s awakened and Ren’s gonna play with us, right? I’ll invite Keel later too!”
And with that, the recording stored in the video crystal came to an end. Having watched the footage, Father placed a hand over his face and shook his head as if in despair.
“I mean, there’s no subscribe button or like button on this thing… who on earth taught Motoyasu-kun those video site catchphrases?”
In one smooth motion, Itsuki raised his hand, drew back his bow, and shot the video crystal clean through. It shattered into countless fragments and scattered into nothing.
“I had a feeling this might be the case… don’t you agree, Ren-san?”
“Yeah. If he’d done all that in that form and just kept quiet about it, I would’ve let it slide.”
“And yet here he is, provoking us like this even after we let it go… No matter what, we’re finding him and stringing him up.”
“Agreed.”
And with that, Ren and Itsuki burst out of my house and took off running.

“You can find some pretty decent-quality materials too, right? Like oreicalcum ore, or geodes.”

Itsuki said, looking toward the room beyond where we’d defeated the boss, I say. In the room ahead… there was a device that played fanfare, a stone monument, and a mural painted on the wall, I say. This dungeon has drops that strengthen equipment called Sacred Weapons and Spirit Tools, so please keep searching, pen. And as a clear reward here, we’ve recorded the method for the limit-breaking Class Up right here, pen. It’s best read after giving a special core stone to the Order Guardian’s kin, the Dragon, pen.』

We hope that this place, all of these islands, and their revitalization will become of help to the Sacred Weapon heroes when the time comes, pen. So, farewell, peeen.』
That’s the text that was engraved there, I say.
“That ‘pen’ ending…”

Ren’s eyes seemed to be bloodshot, I say. Had he really taken such a liking to this place? For what it’s worth, when I asked Father about it, apparently Ren had actually grown quite fond of this dungeon for its excellent experience point yield, I say.

That memory of mine begins on a certain day, I say. Story was that he got killed in some crime-of-passion mess, but he ended up summoned to this world and avoided death that way… still some lingering traces of causal interference from this whole affair’s mastermind. Something about university— oop, that’s edging into someone’s privacy, not really my place to talk about it. Sorry ’bout that.”
So Ho seemed to be talking about matters related to my original world. Terribly irrelevant stuff, honestly.

This Ho person was saying things I couldn’t quite make sense of at all.

Pigs truly are a menace, I say! Ptooey! Indeed, I say!

Was Ho a Filolial-sama or not, I wondered? I approached Ho to conduct my judgment. Sniff, sniff, I say.

Hmm… somehow, it did seem to carry that same rich, fragrant scent found in Filolial-samas. …Though, now that I thought about it, it also somewhat resembled the scent I recalled from when we defeated the Phoenix. Here, Ho pointed accusingly at the cart-pulling Filolial-sama in protest!

The Filolial-samas watched Ho’s refusal of my proposal with what seemed to be genuine concern. There was no need to worry so — no Filolial-sama could truly resist their own instincts, I say.

“Well, it’s exceedingly troublesome, but maybe that’s a good quality too, in its own way.”
In any case, it seemed the apparent boss of the Filolial-samas would be staying in the village for a while, I say.

In other words, the moment an attack made contact, a teleportation skill would shunt it off to some other location—or rather, redirect the trajectory of the attack elsewhere. It reminded me of the Mirror Vassal Weapon Kou possesses, which has a skill that redirects attacks through a mirror.

“The Mirror Vassal Weapon had an attack like that. If it keeps that thing deployed at all times, covering its entire body… there's no way to land a hit through ordinary means. And on top of that, the enemy gets to attack us while shifting its own existence to some other dimension? That’s just cruel.”
A cheat, an exploit—that’s what it amounts to, Father continued.
“If you use something inscribed with the characters I draw, you can cancel out that shift. That way, you’ll be able to properly cut right through them.”
“I see. Well, even if we managed that, whether it’d actually be enough to finish that thing off is another matter.”
“Yeah, probably. From what I heard, it was quite the opponent, so this alone would likely be rough.”
So even breaking through the barrier the Crimson Swine itself deployed wouldn’t be enough to finish it off on its own. Talk about a troublesome enemy, I say.
“By the way, if you apply this magical script, you can also keep your own clothes from catching fire when you unleash some big move. Just shift the space around the clothes alone, and they won’t tear, get dirty, or get wet. Oh, and something this minor won’t get flagged as cheating under this world’s laws.”
“Sounds like it’d be good for the Filolials’ clothes, Motoyasu.”
“Indeed it would! Hou-kun, teach me, I say!”
“Ehh! No way! I don’t really feel like teaching you!”
Hou-kun could be quite cold sometimes, I say.
“Setting up the canceling script isn’t all that hard, but… this world probably doesn’t even need it, does it?”
“…Yeah, probably not.”
Father agreed with Ark’s words. Big Sister nodded quietly as well. Since this world had become peaceful, such technology was simply excessive, I say.
“So it’s the kind of technology that disregards its own proper domain. The sort that the Holy Weapons, the Seven Star Weapons, and the Vassal Weapons would need to keep watch over.”
“I suppose that’s about right.”
And so, in that sort of way, Doctor was learning harmless alchemy techniques from Ark and the others.

Some time had passed since Hou-kun and the others came to the village, I say.
“Hmm… I can’t tell the difference between big bro’s cooking and Ark-san’s cooking anymore.”
Keel muttered this while eating the food served at dinner, I say.
“Well, that’s because I’ve been cooking together with Naofumi-kun.”
“There’s a lot of collaborative dishes too, since he matches my rhythm, it makes things easy.”
After cooking together so many times, Father and the others had apparently gotten the hang of each other’s pace, and now they seemed to cook in perfect sync, I say.
“Nom nom! Naofumi-kun and Kitty’s cooking is so yummy-fu!”
Somehow, Hou-kun was slurping his food with his beak. A steady slurp-slurp rang out, and he seemed to be eating quite happily, I say.
“More importantly, would you quit slurping your food as a bit sometimes.”
“I think maintaining at least a minimum of decency matters, even when you’re doing it as a joke.”
“I don’t know what kind of comedian you’re trying to be, but you should stop eating in a way that makes everyone around you uncomfortable.”
Hou-kun received sub-zero glares from both Father and Ark, but he looked utterly unbothered, as if the wind were simply passing him by.
“It’s delicious, but man, I miss my wife’s cooking.”
Hou-kun longed for the cooking of his wife, who—according to the story—had run away from him, I say.
“Your wife’s seasoning, huh.”
“What kind of taste was it?”
“Hmm, it changed depending on the occasion… but there was a pattern to it. The important thing was the fire, so—”
“Hold on! You don’t need to try recreating it! It feels like my precious memories are about to get overwritten, so just stop already!”
As if pleading with them to quit, Hou-kun cautioned Father and Ark. Indeed, Father was extremely skilled at recreating dishes—he could easily reproduce the taste of any restaurant. Ark seemed to have skills rivaling Father’s as well, so if the two of them put their minds to it, I was certain they could surely recreate the seasoning of Hou-kun’s wife that he longed for, I say.
“Honestly, that bird gets annoying sometimes, so maybe we should study his preferred seasoning until he can’t think about anything but food, or just threaten to withhold his favorite meal whenever he says something out of line.”
“Sounds good.”
“Naofumi-sama, I won’t let you say you’ve forgotten that you experimented on Keel-kun behind my back.”
At this, Big Sister spoke up, driving the point home to Father and Ark, who were scheming something wicked, I say. Apparently, because Father’s cooking was so delicious, he had once used Keel as a test subject to see just how far he could push feeding her favorite food. The goal seemed to be finding the balance where Keel wouldn’t overeat but would still feel satisfied, all to boost her motivation even further. Keel had been chosen both for her own personality and as a reward for the motivation and profits she brought in through her popularity, which rivaled even Filo-tan’s. On top of that, it apparently doubled as an experiment to test whether it was even possible, based on information that some reincarnators had been known to brainwash people through cooking…
For the first few days, nothing seemed particularly off about Keel, but before long her behavior gradually began to change. She threw herself into work with unusual intensity, and whenever mealtime rolled around, she would head toward Father with bloodshot eyes, I say. It was right around this point that Big Sister caught on, scolded Father, and the experiment was called off.
“The food big bro made just for me was super delicious, though…”
“Do you have any idea how hard it was to calm Keel-kun down when she wouldn’t stop complaining to me every time the seasoning changed!”
“Well, Raphtalia’s given us a no-go. Still, if the bird gets to be too much of a pain, I’ll keep the research in mind as an option.”
“That’s harsh. Oh, right. Motoyasu-kun~”
“What is it, I say?”
Hou-kun had called out to me, so I went over.
“What? Just because Motoyasu says something doesn’t mean your messy-eating punishment plan is scrapped.”
“Heh, if you think I’d learn my lesson that easily, you’re sorely mistaken. Let’s leave that topic there for now, Motoyasu-kun. You’ve been treating me like some kind of Filolial lately, so I prepared a little something as thanks.”
Hou-kun spread his wings and, using his beak, pulled something out from within them, setting it down in front of me. At first glance, it looked like a plate depicting a Filolial-sama’s backside.
“You probably think it’s just a plain plate and have no idea what it actually is, so let me explain. This is something you hang on the wall, and you hook the bottle cap right here to pop it open.”
With that, Hou-kun pointed to the little hole in the Filolial-sama’s backside with the tip of his wing.
“Whoa… to think you’d go and make such an elaborate joke item just to mess with someone…”
“Your sense of humor’s on par with some scatological old man’s. Is it worse that you made and gave this with clear malicious intent? No… wait, maybe having obvious malice actually makes it better?”
Father and the others seemed rather taken aback.
“Thank you very much, I say!”
Since Hou-kun had made and given me a piece of merchandise modeled after a Filolial-sama, I intended to treasure it no matter what it actually was! Any gift depicting a Filolial-sama was a precious treasure to me. That’s right—Filolial-sama, who took a liking to anything that shone, would sometimes bestow precious treasures upon me as gifts. And since this one came from someone who went around defeating things like the Crimson Swine itself, I would treasure it for the rest of my life, I say.
“No, wait, listen? This thing is meant to be used this way, and you’re supposed to react with either disgust or fury.”
“Thank you so much for making this for me, I say!”
“Wow… the sarcasm completely missed its mark. Watching that bird react like that is honestly hilarious.”
“Once Motoyasu’s designated you an honorary Filolial, nothing you do has any effect, huh… I knew it, but I have to admire just how thorough he is about it.”
At this point, Older Sister, undeterred as ever, came over to Father and the others carrying a bottle of liquor. Lately, rather than simply looking cheerful every day, she wore more of a relieved expression, as though she were savoring the peace with all her heart.
“Naofumi-chan and everyone~ let’s drink together again today~!”
“You get plastered every single day, and yet you never learn, huh.”
“Truly.”
“Older Sister! Hou-kun made me a wall-mounted bottle opener shaped like a Filolial-sama, I say!”
“Oh my? Is that so?”
Older Sister took her bottle and used the gift Hou-kun had given me—now mounted on the wall—to pop the cap open. It was right before that moment—
“Is the Dark Saint Hero here—”
Black Thunder, searching for Ren, entered the dining hall from right behind Older Sister. Just at that perfect moment, Older Sister had popped the cork with a satisfying pok.
